title: Root-N ATE Estimation under Weak Overlap with Finitely Many Propensity Zeros
banked_reason: kernel_substituted@thm:strict-rootn-phase: The delivered theorem is only a strict-phase result for 2<gamma<=3 while the promised explicit all-(beta,eta,gamma) minimax and honest-length frontier is deferred.
gap_reasons: kernel_substituted@thm:strict-rootn-phase: The delivered theorem is only a strict-phase result for 2<gamma<=3 (root-n above beta=1/2 and a nonmatching lower obstruction below), while the promised explicit all-(beta,eta,gamma) minimax and honest-length frontier, gamma=2/less-than-2 regimes, endpoint logarithm, and matching sub-root upper bounds are deferred.

The headline observable root-n theorem for every β>1/2 rests on a vague paraphrase of Mou et al. that does not state the exact estimator, effective-dimension hypothesis, high-probability bound, or mean-squared-error conversion being imported, so the load-bearing upper bound and honest interval are not verified as written.
proof_attempt_summary: The discovery run developed a strict root-n phase theorem for a narrower regular-tail regime and repaired source-transcription defects in its Mou and Robins arguments. D0.5 found that this theorem substitutes for the promised all-parameter matched minimax and honest-interval frontier; a validity consultation confirmed that restoring the missing regimes, rates, and computable interval is the unresolved research program rather than a bounded repair. No Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: The proposal studies the full-population ATE over a global weak-overlap tail class with finitely many separated power zeros and no propensity H\"older restriction. For \(2<\gamma\le3\), a policy-agnostic Sobolev kernel-ridge estimator has uniform mean-squared error \(O(n^{-1})\) for every \(\beta>1/2\), and a risk-calibrated connected interval exists with uniform \(90\%\) coverage and length \(O(n^{-1/2})\). Same-class oracle converses match both orders. For every \(\beta<1/2\), an explicitly chosen strictly overlapping binary subclass gives slower all-procedure risk and connected-length lower bounds, so the strict root-\(n\) phase boundary is one-half. Equality and exact sub-root rates remain open. Mou, Ding, Wainwright, and Bartlett supply the policy-agnostic RKHS engine; the new work is its uniform finite-zero verification, the binary same-class transfer, and the honest-length conclusion. The published universal constant is not numerically calibrated here, so the KRR interval is existential rather than computable.
gap: Published weak-overlap results provide RKHS local moduli, conditional optimal recovery, local-cell interval calibration, clipped-AIPW sufficient conditions, or pointwise and sup-norm response-regression rates. They do not give an unconditional all-procedure risk and worst-case expected-length theorem for the full-population ATE over the declared finite-zero global-tail class.
fill: The project derives the treated and control Gram inequalities from the primitive class, proves strict class extension and nonlinear opportunity-family membership, constructs a total propensity-free integrated local-polynomial estimator, and matches it by same-class all-procedure risk and connected-interval converses. The oracle equality is recorded inside the main theorem, and the unresolved outcome-smoothness boundary is isolated through a finite-zero primal-dual handle.
